$comment: The extras of omx-delay's declaration: what its descriptor, omx-delay.descriptor.json, has no word for (docs/declaration-as-descriptor.md). The two are the folder's hand-written files; tools/gen.mjs generates the rest and writes the travels the descriptor's links resolve to. Its parameters are by reference to omx-contract's delay kernel and bind by name to omx-dsp's instance face. Control order, the descriptor's, is append-only.
summary: Stereo delay up to {max:fxDelayTime} ms: feedback through a tone filter that darkens each repeat, ping-pong, wet/dry mix. Zero latency, real-time safe.
manual: | Taps (engaged read taps of the one delay line) | {range:fxDelayTaps} | {default:fxDelayTaps} |
| Tap 2 time (a share of the delay time) | 1/4 to 3 | {default:tap1Factor} |
| Tap 3 time (a share of the delay time) | 1/4 to 3 | {default:tap2Factor} |
| Tap 4 time (a share of the delay time) | 1/4 to 3 | {default:tap3Factor} |

With one tap the delay is the single-tap echo. Raising Taps adds the second to fourth reads of the same line, each with its own time, gain and pan; the feedback comes from the longest engaged tap, so a pattern repeats as a whole.
Plus the host's bypass. The tone filter holds the same corner at every sample rate, so a session
moved from 48 to 96 kHz sounds the same.

console.$comment: The OpenMixer console draws its delay stage: the echo taps drawn over time, above the delay panel (pingpong and sync latches, timeMs or a synced division, then feedback, mix, tone; sync and division have no parameter here). Its chip shows timeMs. Its overview card carries the delay's controls.
